decisions.reason: The cover has an independent same-message requirement to show accurate final page numbers, which is already fully represented; the Table of Contents update adds no further change.
Correcting Table of Contents page references does not change the policy or reference layout for balancing article endings.
Finalized pagination may provide context for testing, but the Table of Contents correction does not change the required two-page spread behavior.
The Table of Contents page-number basis does not change the article body font family or treatment.
Final article page numbers do not alter category labels, category mappings, or their placement.
The Table of Contents correction does not change advertisement clarity, sizing, trim, or bleed requirements.
The specified articles remain required regardless of the later correction of Table of Contents page numbers.
Using finalized pagination for Table of Contents references does not modify the issue assembly behavior or its Flat Plan reference.
The page-number correction does not affect author names, photos, sources, or placement.
The Table of Contents correction does not change the required digital flipbook PDF deliverable.
Correct article page references do not change the image-quality enhancement requirement.
The Table of Contents update neither resumes nor modifies the deferred print-ready output requirement.
